From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: RFP: segmentation + threat model (draft artifacts attached)

Neha / Dev — forwarding Acme’s request. Draft artifacts attached: network-diagram-v2.png, isolation-matrix.xlsx, threat-model-summary.pdf. Please review for technical accuracy and any operational caveats; call out anything we shouldn’t promise for the hosted product vs Dedicated/Private.

Inline summary for review (high level):

- Isolation model:
  - Hosted (Redwood Cloud): logical tenancy via per-tenant encryption keys + strict namespace separation. We run multi-tenant inference pools with workload-aware routing; sensitive customers can be placed on dedicated pools.
  - Dedicated: tenant-dedicated GPU pools isolated by Kubernetes namespaces and network policies; optional VPC peering for private networking.
  - Private (VPC/On-prem): full customer-managed VPC with customer-controlled subnets and routing; control plane can be run in a hardened management VPC with cross-account roles.

- Network segmentation controls:
  - Control plane / management network separated from inference dataplane; control plane endpoints are accessible only from specific management subnets and via mutual TLS.
  - Egress controls: egress whitelisting at the subnet level and per-cluster egress proxies for monitoring and threat detection.
  - Bastions & jump hosts: for on-prem and VPC deployments, managed bastion sessions + session recording available on request.

- Data handling & storage:
  - KV cache: ephemeral by default for hosted inference; for Private deployments we offer configurable persistence with customer-managed keys.
  - Encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256 at rest with KMS integration (customer KMS supported). HSM-backed key protection for enterprise tiers.

- Threat model highlights & mitigations (summary):
  - Adversarial input (poisoning/evasion): prompt filtering, rate limiting, and content-scanning hooks; customer-defined prompt safety policies.
  - Data exfiltration via model output: output filters, redaction rules, and logging/anomaly detection.
  - Side-channel leakage (timing, cache): constant-time kernels where possible; isolation of hot KV caches per-tenant on dedicated pools; cache TTLs and eviction policies documented in the matrix.
  - Compromised compute nodes: immutable infrastructure, attestation, and automated re-provisioning; node-level encryption keys and limited operator access.

- Operational controls:
  - Audit logs: configurable retention, tamper-evident logs (signed), and integration with SIEMs.
  - Identity: SSO + role-based access; least privilege in management plane; IAM separation between billing/admin and ops.
  - Incident response: runbook links in the attached PDF, SLA for notification, and tabletop support for enterprise engagements.

Please mark up anything that needs technical correction or more precise wording before I send to Acme.

Thanks,
Jonas
[Attachments: network-diagram-v2.png (PNG, 850KB); isolation-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 320KB); threat-model-summary.pdf (PDF, 210KB)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 28 Apr 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segmentation & Threat Model — RFP follow-up

Michael — quick answers inline:

- Will KV cache persistence encrypt to customer KMS/HSM? Yes. For Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS keys (including HSM-backed keys) for all persisted artifacts including KV cache snapshots. We note this in the isolation matrix (column: "KMS scope").

- Recommended TTL and purge process? Default recommended TTL for persisted caches is 6 hours for workloads that require short-term persistence; we recommend 30 minutes for ephemeral inference-only cache patterns. Purge process: automated lifecycle rules + explicit purge API. We include an ops playbook in the PDF with sample lifecycle rules.

- Are cache artifacts included in backup snapshots? Cache persistence is optional; when enabled and if you opt into backups, snapshots can be taken, but by default caches are excluded from long-term backups to reduce attack surface. Backup inclusion is configurable per-customer and we recommend encryption-in-transit + KMS encryption for snapshots when enabled.

I’ll add a short paragraph to the Drive docs to make the defaults explicit. Let me know if you want a 15-min call to walk through the details (Neha / Dev can join).

Best,
Jonas
Enterprise AE — Redwood Inference
